DIC: digital image correlation: estimating material displacement by comparing image texture
IC-GN: inverse compositional Gauss–Newton: an iterative image-alignment solver
IC: inverse compositional, a formulation that composes updates through the reference-image warp
GN: Gauss–Newton, an iterative least-squares optimization method
HORG: histogram of oriented and rotated gradients, the chirality-aware descriptor
HORG-DIC: initialization of digital image correlation using histograms of oriented and rotated gradients
CPM: coarse-to-fine PatchMatch, a multiscale correspondence search
CPM-HOG: coarse-to-fine PatchMatch using histograms of oriented gradients
CPM-WGPU: the WebGPU implementation of coarse-to-fine PatchMatch in this project
DoG: difference of Gaussians, a scale-space response used to detect extrema
DaD: Distilled Reinforcement Learning for Diverse Keypoint Detection, the published detector name
DeDoDe: Detect, Don’t Describe — Describe, Don’t Detect, the published feature-model family
RaCo: ranking and covariance, the learned keypoint detector
XFeat: accelerated features, the published lightweight feature-model name
ALIKED: A Lighter Keypoint and Descriptor Extraction Network via Deformable Transformation, the published model title
LoFTR: local feature transformer, a detector-free correspondence model
EfficientLoFTR: Efficient Local Feature Transformer, the semi-dense correspondence model
WebGPU: the portable graphics and computation interface for graphics processing units
WGPU: the project label for its WebGPU-based implementation; wgpu-py is the Python runtime binding
WGSL: WebGPU Shading Language, the language used for the graphics-processor compute kernels
ONNX: Open Neural Network Exchange, a model interchange format
ORT: ONNX Runtime, the inference engine for Open Neural Network Exchange models
EP: execution provider, a runtime backend that executes model operations
IOBinding: input/output binding, a runtime mechanism for explicitly binding model buffers
ROI: region of interest, the image area allowed for analysis
POI: point of interest, a requested location for displacement initialization
NMS: non-maximum suppression, retaining local peaks while suppressing neighbouring responses
RANSAC: random sample consensus, robust model fitting by testing sampled subsets
RBF: radial basis function, a function depending on distance from a centre
TPS: thin-plate spline, a smooth radial-basis interpolation model
ECC: enhanced correlation coefficient, the photometric alignment objective used here
LOO: leave one out, fitting without one observation to check its prediction
FPS: frames per second; these pair benchmarks count complete image-pair calls per second
P95: 95th percentile: the value below which 95 percent of the measured observations fall
UHD: ultra-high definition; the tensile images here have 3840 × 2160 pixels
4K: a resolution class around four thousand pixels in width; exact image dimensions must also be given
8K: a resolution class around eight thousand pixels in width; exact image dimensions must also be given
RGB: red, green and blue colour channels
NCHW: batch, channels, height, width: a tensor-axis order
NHWC: batch, height, width, channels: a tensor-axis order
BCE: binary cross entropy, a classification loss
BLAS: Basic Linear Algebra Subprograms, optimized routines for dense vector and matrix operations
KL: Kullback–Leibler divergence, a measure of difference between probability distributions
InfoNCE: information noise-contrastive estimation, a contrastive learning objective for matching positive pairs against distractors
MLP: multilayer perceptron, a fully connected neural network
SiLU: sigmoid linear unit, the activation x multiplied by sigmoid(x)
SELU: scaled exponential linear unit, a neural-network activation
RSS: resident set size, the process memory currently resident in physical memory
H2D: host-to-device transfer, from processor memory to graphics-device memory
D2H: device-to-host transfer, from graphics-device memory to processor memory
CSV: comma-separated values, a tabular text format
JSON: JavaScript Object Notation, a structured text format
NPZ: compressed NumPy archive storing named arrays
HTML: HyperText Markup Language, the format of the compiled web pages
PNG: Portable Network Graphics, a lossless image format
GIF: Graphics Interchange Format, used here for alternating-image animations
SHA-256: Secure Hash Algorithm with a 256-bit digest, used to identify exact model files
SHA: Secure Hash Algorithm, a family of cryptographic file-digest algorithms
PIL: Python Imaging Library; image handling here uses its maintained successor Pillow
URL: uniform resource locator, a web address
CI: continuous integration, automated checks triggered by repository changes
RTD: Read the Docs, the documentation hosting service and theme family
INRIA: Institut national de recherche en informatique et en automatique, the French research institute associated with DeepMatching
CVPR: Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition
MIT: Massachusetts Institute of Technology; MIT License names the associated permissive software licence
GPL: GNU General Public License, a copyleft software licence
GNU: GNU’s Not Unix, the free-software project name
EOG: Eye of GNOME, the image viewer used for local comparisons
GNOME: GNU Network Object Model Environment, the desktop project name
LNL: Lunar Lake, the Intel graphics-platform codename in the measurements
L1: sum of absolute component values, used as a distance or norm
L2: Euclidean norm, the square root of the sum of squared components
P0: phase zero, the initial diagnostic stage of the development schedule
P1: phase one, the first implementation stage of the development schedule
DINOv2: a self-supervised visual-feature backbone; the model name refers to the second DINO generation
SfM: structure from motion, reconstructing scene geometry and camera poses from multiple images
MVS: multi-view stereo, estimating scene depth from several calibrated images
PyPI: Python Package Index, the public Python package repository
ZNCC: zero-normalized cross correlation, comparing mean-centred and variance-normalized image intensities
ZNSSD: zero-normalized sum of squared differences, a normalized photometric mismatch objective
LK: Lucas–Kanade, an iterative local image-alignment method
PDF: Portable Document Format, the fixed-layout format of the printed handbook
A4: a paper format measuring 210 by 297 millimetres
POIs: points of interest, requested locations for displacement initialization
TIFF: Tagged Image File Format, an image container format
